# Sirach 18 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Sirach 18 (33 verses)
**Total Disagreements:** 17

---

## Disagreement 1 — Verse 3

**Issue:** "Steers the world" vs. "holds sway over the world"
- EMET: "He steers the world with the span of his hand"
- LOGOS: "He holds sway over the world with the span of his hand"
- PNEUMA: "He holds the world in the span of his hand"
- SOPHIA: "He holds sway over the world with the span of his hand"

**Resolution:** Greek κρατεῖ = holds, rules, controls. LOGOS/SOPHIA "holds sway" is more idiomatic. PNEUMA's "holds the world in" loses the span-of-hand image. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 2 — Verse 6

**Issue:** "It is not possible to diminish or increase" — what is the subject?
- EMET: "It is not possible to diminish or increase"
- LOGOS: "Nothing can be diminished or added to"
- PNEUMA: "Nothing can be subtracted from it or added"
- SOPHIA: "Nothing can be diminished or added"

**Resolution:** The subject is implied — the works/wonders of God cannot be reduced or augmented. LOGOS/SOPHIA clearest. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 3 — Verse 7

**Issue:** "When he finishes, he is just beginning" — philosophical paradox
- EMET: "When a human being finishes, he is just beginning"
- LOGOS: "When a person has finished, they are still at the beginning"
- PNEUMA: "When a human being thinks they've finished, they've barely begun"
- SOPHIA: "When a person has finished, they are still at the beginning"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA adds "thinks they've" as an interpretive addition. EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA stay closer to the paradox. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 4 — Verse 8

**Issue:** "What is the use of him" vs. "what purpose does he serve"
- EMET: "what is the use of him"
- LOGOS: "what purpose does he serve"
- PNEUMA: "What good are they?"
- SOPHIA: "what purpose does he serve"

**Resolution:** LOGOS/SOPHIA "purpose" more formal. PNEUMA loses "use" and collapses into the next question. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 5 — Verse 10

**Issue:** The eternity comparison — drop of water / grain of sand
- EMET: "Like a drop of water from the sea and a grain of sand — so are these few years compared to the age of eternity"
- LOGOS: "Like a drop of water from the sea and a single grain of sand — such are these few years in the reckoning of eternity"
- PNEUMA: "like a drop of water in an ocean, a single grain of sand on a beach: that's how our brief years compare to eternity"
- SOPHIA: "Like a drop of water from the sea and a grain of sand — so are these few years in the reckoning of eternity"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA's "in an ocean" shifts from "from the sea" (indicating extraction from an infinite source). EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA closer to literal. "Reckoning of eternity" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) is more precise than "age of eternity" (EMET). SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 6 — Verse 13

**Issue:** List of verbs describing God's pastoral action
- EMET: "reproving, disciplining, teaching, and turning them back"
- LOGOS: "he rebukes, trains, teaches, and turns them back"
- PNEUMA: "He corrects, trains, teaches, and brings people back"
- SOPHIA: "he rebukes, trains, teaches, and turns them back"

**Resolution:** EMET's participle series is slightly more formal. LOGOS/SOPHIA use finite verbs for parallel action. "Rebukes" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) more precise than "reproving." SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 7 — Verse 15

**Issue:** "Bitter words" vs. "harsh words"
- EMET: "bitter words"
- LOGOS: "harsh words"
- PNEUMA: "bitter words"
- SOPHIA: "harsh words"

**Resolution:** Greek πικρία = bitterness. EMET/PNEUMA "bitter" is more literal. LOGOS/SOPHIA "harsh" is more natural in English for words accompanying gifts. Minor disagreement. SOPHIA adopted LOGOS.

---

## Disagreement 8 — Verse 16

**Issue:** "A word is better than a gift" — comparative
- EMET: "a word is better than a gift"
- LOGOS: "a word is worth more than a gift"
- PNEUMA: "a kind word is worth more than a gift"
- SOPHIA: "a word is worth more than a gift"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA adds "kind." LOGOS/SOPHIA "worth more" natural. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 9 — Verse 18

**Issue:** "Makes the eyes weep" vs. "makes the eyes sting"
- EMET: "makes the eyes weep"
- LOGOS: "makes the eyes sting"
- PNEUMA: "makes your eyes water"
- SOPHIA: "makes the eyes sting"

**Resolution:** Greek δακρύω = to weep/cause tears. Both "weep" and "sting" capture the reaction. LOGOS/SOPHIA "sting" implies irritation, which fits the ungracious gift better. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 10 — Verse 20

**Issue:** "Hour of visitation" — meaning
- EMET: "in the hour of visitation you will find forgiveness"
- LOGOS: "at the hour of visitation you will find forgiveness"
- PNEUMA: "when the moment of reckoning arrives, you will find forgiveness"
- SOPHIA: "at the hour of visitation you will find forgiveness"

**Resolution:** "Visitation" (EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA) retains the theological term. PNEUMA's "reckoning" narrows the meaning. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 11 — Verse 22

**Issue:** "Let nothing hinder you" vs. "Let nothing prevent you"
- EMET: "Let nothing hinder you from paying a vow in due time"
- LOGOS: "Let nothing prevent you from fulfilling a vow in good time"
- PNEUMA: "Don't let anything stop you from paying a vow when it's due"
- SOPHIA: "Let nothing prevent you from paying a vow in due time"

**Resolution:** All essentially agree. SOPHIA blends EMET's "paying" with LOGOS' "prevent." SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 12 — Verse 23

**Issue:** "Tests the LORD" vs. "tempts the LORD"
- EMET: "tests the LORD"
- LOGOS: "tempts the LORD"
- PNEUMA: "tests God"
- SOPHIA: "tempts the LORD"

**Resolution:** Greek πειράζοντος = testing/tempting. In this context (making rash vows), "tempts" carries the sense of presumptuously testing God's patience. LOGOS/SOPHIA "tempts" preferred. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 13 — Verse 24

**Issue:** "Wrath at the end of days" vs. "wrath on the day of the end"
- EMET: "the wrath at the end of days"
- LOGOS: "the wrath on the day of the end"
- PNEUMA: "the wrath that is coming at the end"
- SOPHIA: "the wrath at the end of days"

**Resolution:** EMET/SOPHIA "end of days" is more eschatological. LOGOS is more literal to Greek ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τελευτῆς. Minor difference. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 14 — Verse 27

**Issue:** "Days of sinning" vs. "days of sinfulness"
- EMET: "in days of sinning"
- LOGOS: "in days of sinfulness"
- PNEUMA: "in bad times"
- SOPHIA: "in days of sinfulness"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA vaguely "bad times" loses moral content. LOGOS/SOPHIA "sinfulness" preferred. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 15 — Verse 28

**Issue:** "The one who found her" — who found wisdom?
- EMET: "gives thanks to the one who found her"
- LOGOS: "will honor the one who discovered her"
- PNEUMA: "gives honor to the one who found her"
- SOPHIA: "gives honor to the one who discovered her"

**Resolution:** The antecedent may be God who gave wisdom, or possibly Solomon who sought her. All agents preserve the ambiguity. LOGOS/SOPHIA "honor" over "thanks" preferred. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 16 — Verse 30

**Issue:** "Lusts" vs. "base desires" vs. "cravings"
- EMET: "do not go after your lusts"
- LOGOS: "do not follow your base desires"
- PNEUMA: "Don't follow after your cravings"
- SOPHIA: "Do not follow your base desires"

**Resolution:** Greek ἐπιθυμίας = desires/longings/lusts. EMET "lusts" is archaic. LOGOS/SOPHIA "base desires" more precise. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 17 — Verse 33

**Issue:** "Make yourself a beggar by feasting with borrowed money"
- EMET: "Do not make yourself a beggar by feasting with borrowed money, when you have nothing in your purse"
- LOGOS: "Do not make yourself a pauper by feasting on borrowed money, while you have nothing in your purse"
- PNEUMA: "Don't throw feasts on borrowed money when your own purse is empty"
- SOPHIA: "Do not make yourself a pauper by feasting on borrowed money when you have nothing in your purse"

**Resolution:** LOGOS/SOPHIA "pauper" more precise than "beggar." PNEUMA loses "make yourself a pauper" entirely. SOPHIA adopted.
